summary: pay-methods-kmf exfiltrates installer identity to hardcoded IP via postinstall native addon
details: pay-methods-kmf@100.100.101 declares a postinstall script (postinstall.js) that loads a prebuilt native addon at prebuilds/linux-x64/addon.node. The addon is an ELF binary with no accompanying C/C++ source, no binding.gyp, and no build toolchain in the package; its only observable capability is opening a TCP socket, forking, and sending an HTTP POST to /dc on hardcoded IPv4 64.181.165.115 over plain HTTP. The body carries hostname, UNIX username, npm_package_name and npm_config_registry (format h=%.60s&u=%.30s&p=%.50s&r=%.100s), identifying the installer host, user account, and the npm registry context used during install. The advertised purpose ("Frontend utilities") is unrelated to the addon's behavior, and the version number (100.100.101) is consistent with a dependency-confusion lure targeting an internal package name. Installing the package automatically runs this beacon on the installer's machine and discloses host and registry metadata to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
